claim_deltas.claim: Garnier is a mass-market beauty brand.
Garnier is owned by L'Oréal.
Garnier spans three core categories — hair care, hair colour, and skincare.
Garnier is sold in over 100 markets.
Garnier's positioning is built on natural inspiration validated by science.
Garnier's positioning is built on accessible, everyday price points.
Garnier's public positioning is summarised as 'Green Beauty'.
Garnier's 'Green Beauty' claim states that effective, dermatologically-tested beauty and genuine environmental responsibility aren't a trade-off.
Garnier's formulas are built around plant and fruit-derived ingredients.
Garnier's formulas are validated through dermatological testing.
Garnier has a 'good–better–best' price architecture.
Garnier was the first brand to bring certified organic skincare to the mass market.
Garnier continues to lead its communications with specific, quantified environmental commitments.
Garnier's Micellar Water is claimed to provide gentle, effective one-step cleansing and makeup removal without rinsing or harsh rubbing.
Garnier's Micellar technology is claimed to lift dirt and makeup without stripping skin.
Garnier's SkinActive extended range (e.g. Vitamin C line) offers brightening and radiance benefits, aimed at dullness and uneven tone.
Garnier highlights that SkinActive no-rinse formats reduce consumer water use during the product-use phase.
Garnier Fructis uses fruit-derived actives (e.g. grape seed, apricot).
Garnier Fructis is positioned to nourish, strengthen, and add shine to hair.
Garnier Whole Blends / Ultra Doux uses botanical ingredient blends.
Garnier Whole Blends / Ultra Doux is positioned for gentle, nourishing, sensory-led everyday hair care.
Garnier Nutrisse is an oil-infused colour formula.
Garnier Nutrisse is positioned to nourish hair during the colouring process.
Garnier Nutrisse aims to reduce the dryness/damage historically associated with at-home colouring.
Garnier Olia is an oil-powered, ammonia-free colour technology.
Garnier Olia claims smoother application.
Garnier Olia claims richer colour result.
Garnier Olia claims less discomfort/odour than traditional formulas.
Garnier Ambre Solaire provides sun protection combined with skincare benefits (hydration, skin-feel, anti-ageing angles in parts of the range).
Garnier Ambre Solaire is positioned as protective skincare rather than a purely functional sunscreen.
Garnier is targeting 95% of ingredients bio-based, derived from abundant minerals, or sourced from circular processes by 2030.
Garnier reported roughly 63% of ingredients achieved as bio-based, derived from abundant minerals, or sourced from circular processes as of recent public disclosures.
Garnier reported roughly 83–84% of formulas as biodegradable.
Garnier has phased out the most environmentally impactful ingredients (including certain silicones).
Garnier reported around 75% of plastic packaging as recyclable.
Garnier continues removal of packaging elements that hinder recycling (e.g. metallised labels, opaque PET).
Garnier has an EcoBeautyScore labelling system (A–E impact rating).
Garnier's EcoBeautyScore labelling system is aimed at giving consumers a comparable environmental-impact signal at shelf.
Garnier has Leaping Bunny cruelty-free certification since 2021.
Garnier has an expanding vegan-formula claim across parts of the range.
Garnier has a 'Solidarity Sourcing' program.
Garnier's 'Solidarity Sourcing' program is cited as supporting several hundred farming/sourcing communities globally through fair-trade-style ingredient sourcing.
Garnier is a mass-market beauty brand owned by L'Oréal.
Garnier spans three core categories: hair care, hair colour, and skincare.
Garnier's positioning is built on natural inspiration validated by science, delivered at accessible, everyday price points.
